themes: AI data-center power demand is a durable structural driver, favoring independent power producers (VST, CEG, NRG) with contracted capacity and grid-scale flexibility.
US IRA tax-credit clarity and domestic supply-chain reshoring continue to de-risk solar and storage names (SEDG, ARRY, CWEN), supporting margin recovery into 2026.

sectors.ai: Buy the US-listed renewables complex on relative strength; ID names lag but signal is NORMAL, not bearish. Rotate into SEDG, MPOW, and VST for momentum, while adding VST and CEG as core power-demand plays. Avoid chasing ID weakness; wait for a catalyst. sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Small-cap consumer stocks are decoupling from large-cap FMCG, driven by domestic retail investor flows and low-float dynamics, creating persistent alpha opportunities.
Regulatory and import-substitution tailwinds are favoring local brands (e.g., BIKE, POLU) over multinationals, a structural shift in Indonesia's consumer preference.
Volatility in the rupiah and input costs will keep pressuring margin-heavy staples, but agile, niche players with pricing power will outperform the sector average.
sectors.ai: Buy selective momentum names (BIKE, POLU, AGAR) but trim broad FMCG exposure; the sector's -0.77% aggregate masks a sharp divergence—small-cap consumer plays are rallying on domestic liquidity while large caps lag. Rotate into high-beta names with volume confirmation, avoid index-heavy staples until IDX stabilizes.

Packaging and construction-material names (PACK, PICO) face structural overcapacity and weak private capex, capping upside despite today's idiosyncratic spikes.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in tower and gas infrastructure names (TOWR, RGAS) on Indonesia's structural digitalization and energy-transition capex; avoid packaging and construction laggards (PACK, PICO) where margin compression persists. Rotate from US-exposed plays into domestic ID beneficiaries as rupiah stabilizes and Jokowi's successor front-loads infrastructure spending.

sectors.name: Healthcare
themes: Indonesia's universal health coverage (JKN) expansion is structurally lifting outpatient volumes and private clinic utilization, benefiting MTMH and RSGK regardless of quarterly noise.
Aging demographics and rising non-communicable disease prevalence in Indonesia are driving durable demand for diagnostic and specialist care, underpinning DGNS and PRAY's growth runway.
US healthcare services names (UNH, CNC) offer defensive cash flows but face regulatory headwinds, making them tactical hedges rather than core Indonesian healthcare exposure.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian healthcare names with domestic revenue and margin resilience—MTMH, DGNS, RSGK—on pullbacks, as the sector's -1.31% ID dip is idiosyncratic, not systemic; US exposure (UNH, CNC) adds diversification but not alpha. Favor operators with clinic expansion and insurance-linked volume growth over pharma distributors; trim on any 5%+ rally without earnings confirmation.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: Indonesia's toll-road connectivity expansion is structurally raising demand for integrated logistics and warehousing, benefiting operators like CMNP and MITI with direct infrastructure exposure.
E-commerce penetration in Indonesia remains underpenetrated versus GDP per capita, driving sustained parcel volume growth that favors last-mile and cold-chain players such as SAFE and PSSI.
Global supply chain diversification is accelerating US logistics outsourcing, with FDX and GXO gaining from nearshoring and automation investments that improve yield per shipment.
sectors.ai: Buy the dip in Indonesia logistics leaders (SAFE, PPGL, MITI) as domestic volume growth and toll-road capex outpace the aggregate decline; US names (FDX, GXO) offer defensive upside on e-commerce restocking. Rotate out of laggards with weak cash conversion, and add on any further 1-2% sector weakness.
